Not sure these are from your commit, but can you see if these are valid?

Warning: epan/dissectors/packet-gsm_sim.c : value_string mf_dfs - value  12037 repeated with different values - was "EF.ELP" now "EF.PL"

Warning: epan/dissectors/packet-gsm_sim.c hf_select_return_data filter= gsm_sim.select.return_data  - mask with non-contiguous bits 0x9C ( 0x9c )

Note: epan/dissectors/packet-gsm_sim.c hf_tp_soft_key_info_max_nb filter= gsm_sim.tp.soft_key_info.max_nb  - mask is all set - if only want value (rather than bits), set 0 instead? : "0xff"

Warning: epan/dissectors/packet-gsm_sim.c:1920 proto_tree_add_item called for FT_UINT32 field "hf_fcp_prop_avail_memory"  - with bad encoding - "ENC_NA" - {'ENC_BIG_ENDIAN', 'ENC_LITTLE_ENDIAN', 'ENC_HOST_ENDIAN'} allowed

Warning: epan/dissectors/packet-gsm_sim.c:1927 proto_tree_add_item called for FT_UINT32 field "hf_fcp_prop_reserved_file_size"  - with bad encoding - "ENC_NA" - {'ENC_BIG_ENDIAN', 'ENC_LITTLE_ENDIAN', 'ENC_HOST_ENDIAN'} allowed

Warning: epan/dissectors/packet-gsm_sim.c:1930 proto_tree_add_item called for FT_UINT32 field "hf_fcp_prop_max_file_size"  - with bad encoding - "ENC_NA" - {'ENC_BIG_ENDIAN', 'ENC_LITTLE_ENDIAN', 'ENC_HOST_ENDIAN'} allowed

Some are from the previous commit, some are older. I'll have a look.

Unfortunately the tools/check_dissector.py gives me an error:
```
RuntimeError: 
        An attempt has been made to start a new process before the
        current process has finished its bootstrapping phase.

        This probably means that you are not using fork to start your
        child processes and you have forgotten to use the proper idiom
        in the main module:

            if __name__ == '__main__':
                freeze_support()
                ...

        The "freeze_support()" line can be omitted if the program
        is not going to be frozen to produce an executable.

        To fix this issue, refer to the "Safe importing of main module"
        section in https://docs.python.org/3/library/multiprocessing.html
```

Oh dear, I will check.

I do have a bug fix to check_typed_item_calls.py in another branch, not sure if it'll fix this or not.
I don't get this error when running tools/check_dissector.py.  Is there more context you can share, maybe a call stack?
